title: Mid-Term Premium True-Down for Shrinking Payrolls
one_liner: Monitor payroll against the estimate on a small business's workers' comp and liability policy, and file mid-term endorsements to cut inflated installments and misclassified codes.
customer: Small businesses with 10-200 employees and volatile payroll (trades, restaurants, staffing, light manufacturing) that already run payroll on Gusto, ADP, Rippling or QuickBooks, reached through CPAs and bookkeepers.
problem: Workers' comp and general liability premiums are priced on estimated payroll and revenue, and only reconciled at year-end audit. When headcount drops, the business keeps paying installments on inflated estimates, financing the insurer, often through premium finance at rising interest. Class-code misclassification (office staff coded as field staff) is also common. Brokers are paid a percentage of premium, so nobody is paid to lower it mid-term.
solution: Connect payroll data, compare actual payroll by class code with the policy estimate each month, generate the carrier endorsement request and support documents, and track the reduced installment schedule. Audit class codes and prepare audit-ready records. Offer optional pay-as-you-go workers' comp placement later.
why_now: Hiring freezes and layoffs are rising as the economy cools. Higher rates raise the cost of premium financing and make cash tighter. Payroll APIs are mature enough to automate the variance check.
revenue_model: 20% of the first-year realized premium reduction, or $49-99 per month SaaS. Partnerships with CPA firms and bookkeepers.
non_obvious_insight: The blocker is incentives, not technology. Brokers earn commission on premium, so no one in the chain is paid to file the endorsement. Downturns make the savings largest exactly when cash is scarcest.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 small businesses through two CPA or bookkeeper networks. Review each policy's declarations page against the last three months of payroll. File endorsements and misclassification challenges by hand, record the realized savings and set pricing at 20% of the first-year benefit.

title: Quibi for Home-Care Aides: Serialized Compliance Training
one_liner: Quibi's 90-second premium episodes failed as a consumer subscription; as a serialized vertical drama that home-care aides watch to fulfill their mandatory annual training hours, the same format has a captive, budgeted buyer.
customer: Owners and training directors of home-health and home-care agencies with 20-500 aides. Medicare-certified home health agencies must give each aide annual in-service training (12 hours under federal rules), and many states add annual hours for personal-care aides.
problem: Caregiver turnover benchmarks around 75% in 2025. Required training is slide decks and quizzes that workers click through on phones, yet client falls, infections, abuse-reporting failures and survey citations trace back to it. Agencies pay for training that neither sticks nor improves retention.
solution: A private serialized story of two aides and a difficult client. Each 90-second vertical episode ends on a decision (dementia sundowning, family conflict, suspected neglect); the answer unlocks the next episode. Delivered by SMS or WhatsApp link with no app, in English, Spanish, Tagalog and Haitian Creole. An RN advisor approves content, quiz logs map to training-hour documentation, and supervisors get a completion dashboard. AI-assisted production plus human voice actors keeps a season at low tens of thousands of dollars.
why_now: Microdrama apps are booming: industry trackers put short-drama in-app revenue near $3B in 2025 and forecasts of roughly $8B in 2026, so the habit and format exist. Reported AI-assisted production budgets of $15-80k per series are far below traditional costs. Home-care demand is surging while the workforce shrinks.
revenue_model: $6-10 per aide per month with a $300/mo agency minimum, annual contracts; bespoke episodes on an agency's own policies at $3-5k each; same engine later sold to nursing homes, restaurants and hotels.
non_obvious_insight: Quibi's format was fine and its buyer was wrong. Consumers would not pay $8/mo for premium clips, but mandatory compliance budgets are captive and the outcomes (completion, quiz retention, incident reports, quits) are measurable. Frontline workers already binge microdramas on the same phones, so the drama does the engagement work and the compliance layer does the billing.
first_30_days: Write 6 episodes on three topics (dementia behaviors, fall prevention, abuse reporting) with an RN advisor and produce them for under $5k. Pitch 30 agencies through state home-care association lists and LinkedIn. Run free 30-day pilots at 3 agencies, comparing completion and quiz scores against their current slides, then convert to $500/mo contracts.

title: Collateral Condition Reports for Farm Equipment
one_liner: Use newly opened Deere diagnostics to certify used-equipment condition for lenders and auctioneers handling a farm-distress wave.
customer: Community ag banks, Farm Credit associations, equipment auction houses and receivers.
problem: Farm bankruptcies are up 19% and row crops face a fourth loss-making year, so lenders are inheriting machinery they cannot value; poor condition data drives lowball auctions.
solution: An inspection product that reads fault history, engine and hydraulic hours and software status through independent diagnostic tools and issues a per-unit condition certificate, then builds valuation comps.
why_now: Deere's $99M settlement obliges it to open diagnostic and repair tools for 10 years, and repair restrictions cost farmers about $4.2B a year, so independent access is finally legitimate.
revenue_model: $250-600 per report, with annual subscriptions for lenders and per-lot fees from auction houses.
non_obvious_insight: Right-to-repair is framed as a farmer-savings story, but its most bankable use is collateral valuation for the lenders and auctioneers who must price distress.
first_30_days: Partner with three Midwest auction houses and two community banks, run 20 paid inspections using existing independent diagnostic tools, and publish sale-price comparisons.

title: Code-Cleared Church Space for Microschools
one_liner: Pair congregations with empty classroom wings and microschool or childcare operators, and sell the missing piece: pre-cleared zoning, fire and licensing paths.
customer: Microschool founders, learning-pod operators and small childcare providers who pay rent, and shrinking congregations, lodges and libraries with weekday space. Operators pay a platform fee; congregations pay for readiness passports.
problem: Microschool enrollment has grown an estimated 40% since 2023, and ESAs plus a federal scholarship tax credit starting in 2027 will add demand. Space is not the constraint; permission is. Certificate-of-occupancy, fire-marshal, egress, sprinkler and childcare-licensing rules vary by jurisdiction, so operators guess and congregations do not know what their building could legally host.
solution: For each listed building, produce a jurisdiction-specific readiness passport: occupancy class, likely deficiencies with cost estimates, pre-drawn plan sets, checklist and sequencing for approvals. Add a standard lease, child-protection policy pack and insurance bundle. Operators search by county and see how many weeks and dollars separate them from opening.
why_now: ESAs, tax-credit scholarships and state laws (Florida now lets registered microschools use former churches and similar buildings without zoning changes) are moving faster than building codes. Congregations are shrinking and buildings are costly to maintain. Treasury rulemaking on what counts as a school adds uncertainty that rewards jurisdiction-specific expertise.
revenue_model: $2k to $6k per building readiness passport, 5% of first-year rent or $250 to $500 a month platform fee from operators, insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Listing space is a commodity. Pre-cleared certainty is the product, and the code-path knowledge compounds jurisdiction by jurisdiction. Each solved county becomes a reusable playbook and a barrier to competitors.
first_30_days: Pick one state that has ESAs and friendly rules (Florida, Texas, Arizona or Tennessee). Map the approval path in 3 counties. Sign 5 churches and 5 microschool operators through founder groups. Deliver the first paid passport for $3k with a code consultant.

title: Tariff Exposure Radar by House Plan
one_liner: A per-plan bill-of-materials scan that flags the small imported, tariff-exposed slice of inputs, prices the swing and proposes lower-exposure substitutes.
customer: Purchasing managers and owners at regional and mid-size builders (100-2,000 homes a year), remodelers, and building-material dealers. Distribution via home builders associations.
problem: NAHB estimates tariffs add $10,900 per home and Brookings sees about $30B added to residential construction and renovation cost by 2027. Only about 7% of inputs are imported, but they are mostly items with no quick domestic substitute, and reported lumber and steel tariff rates conflict across sources. Builders reprice by gut, sign fixed-price contracts blind, and have no per-plan exposure number.
solution: Ingest plan takeoffs and supplier price lists, map each SKU to country of origin and tariff line, and compute exposure per plan and per option package. Deliver escalation-clause language for buyer and sub contracts, alerts when rates change, substitute suggestions from domestic or alternate-origin catalogs, and a group-buy on substitutes.
why_now: Tariff rates are moving and sources disagree. Builder margins are gone (63% use incentives), so a $10K per-home swing decides whether a plan pencils. Structured plan data is now available from design-automation tools.
revenue_model: $500-2,000 per month per builder. $1,500 one-off plan audits. 2-4% rebate on substituted spend from group buys.
non_obvious_insight: Because most of a house is domestic, the tariff burden is a short list of SKUs, so the right tool is a narrow, boring lookup rather than a global trade-compliance platform. The money is in plan-level re-spec and escalation clauses, not in customs filings.
first_30_days: Offer 10 builders a free top-40 exposed-SKU audit from their last three takeoffs and supplier quotes. Send a one-page report and convert 3 to paid. Get a slot in a regional builders association newsletter.

title: Bereavement Aftercare for Independent Funeral Homes
one_liner: A white-label 13-month aftercare program that funeral homes buy to keep the newly widowed connected after the casseroles stop.
customer: Independent funeral homes (roughly 18,000 in the US, mostly independent), paying $200-350 per family served or a flat monthly fee.
problem: Grief tech money chases griefbots and digital memorials. The real gap is months 2-13, when widowhood drives isolation, depression and elevated mortality. Funeral directors hold the only list of newly bereaved households and a position of trust, but 'aftercare' is usually a brochure and a card. Cremation rates above 60% shrink revenue per call, and independents need loyalty and pre-need referrals to survive against consolidators.
solution: A packaged program: scheduled outreach calls at day 3, 14, 30 and 90, plus first-holiday and anniversary contacts. Small 'second-Thursday' peer groups hosted in the funeral home's own room. A paperwork concierge for Social Security, pensions and accounts, which is the logistics half of grief. A prolonged-grief screener at 6 months with referral to partner clinicians. Software runs scripts, scheduling, facilitator rosters and flags.
why_now: WHO's 2025 framing of loneliness as a measured global health metric gives directors a vocabulary and a reason to act. Rising cremation share squeezes revenue per family. Boomer-parent deaths are rising. Independents are hunting a differentiator against Service Corporation International-style chains.
revenue_model: $200-350 per family served billed to the funeral home, plus referral fees from partner therapists and an uplift in pre-need sales the home can attribute to the program.
non_obvious_insight: Griefbot founders sell to the bereaved at their worst moment. The natural customer for grief is the funeral director, who owns the list, is paid nothing after day 3, and buys aftercare as a marketing and retention expense at his best moment.
first_30_days: Sell 5 funeral homes at $300 per family through state funeral-director association meetings. Hire two part-time facilitators (hospice social workers). Run the first second-Thursday group. Track 6-month contact retention and pre-need referrals as the proof for the next 50 homes.

title: Payday-Shaped Pix Automático Cadence for Low-Income Billers
one_liner: A layer on top of Brazilian gateways that designs the recurring-debit cadence (weekly, biweekly, payday-aligned) and consent options at enrollment, so small billers stop losing all-or-nothing monthly debits.
customer: Small Brazilian businesses billing low-income or irregular-income payers on a recurring basis: neighborhood ISPs, small gyms, neighborhood schools, discount-card clinics, motorbike-rental fleets for delivery couriers (to validate first), and insurance or consórcio sellers. They pay 10-15% of incremental collected revenue.
problem: Pix Automático collects the full amount or nothing, with no partial debits. Retries are limited to 3 in 7 days and only if the payer consented. The payer can cancel or edit the mandate up to the eve of the debit, and the mandate cannot change frequency or amount ceiling after authorization. Meanwhile 83.9 million Brazilians were in negative credit standing in August 2026, a record. Monthly lump debits collide with irregular income, and small merchants still chase payers by hand every month.
solution: At enrollment, quote cadence from the payer's income rhythm (weekly for app-paid couriers and informal workers, biweekly for 'vale' and salary splits, monthly for salaried payers) and create the correct mandate with retries-consent and, optionally, credit-line consent. A WhatsApp 'pre-debit rescue' 48-72 hours before each charge lets the payer confirm, move the date to just after payday, pause, or split into a new mandate, instead of silently cancelling in the bank app. Built as an API layer over a gateway that already exposes the retry policy, such as Asaas. Reports per merchant show debit success rate, cancellation reasons and recovered revenue.
why_now: Pix Automático launched in June 2025 and adoption is compounding. Companies had to be able to offer it from 1 Jan 2026, and it is far cheaper than cards and has no chargebacks. About 60% of low-income Brazilians lack credit cards, so account-debit is the only recurring rail for that segment. Most tooling so far is generic dunning, not cadence design.
revenue_model: Performance-based: 10-15% of incremental collected revenue versus the merchant's baseline, or a flat R$149/month for merchants who prefer subscription. Later a per-debit micro-fee and a marketplace of payer-side 'payday buffers'.
non_obvious_insight: The frequency is locked at authorization, so cadence is an irreversible, high-leverage decision at signup, and nobody optimizes it. Because partial collection is not allowed, the only way to fit a low-income payer's cashflow is to change the shape of the debits, not to chase them afterwards. Evidence: PagBrasil reports +182% transactions and +181% new users quarter over quarter from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026, and a coffee subscriber cut churn 25.2% and cost 50% versus cards (https://www.pagbrasil.com/blog/recurring-payments/automatic-pix-2026/). Serasa reported 83.9 million negativados in August 2026 (https://www.shipay.com.br/inadimplencia-no-brasil-como-melhorar-cobrancas/). Rules on no partials, 3 retries in 7 days and cancellation until the day before are at https://celcoin.com.br/articles/vale-a-pena-pix-automatico/ and https://docs.asaas.com/docs/faq-2. The mandate 'cannot change the frequency' and 60% of low-income Brazilians lack cards (https://www.pymnts.com/news/payments-innovation/2025/pix-automatico-debut-opens-brazils-recurring-payments-market-to-millions/). Small billers describe the monthly grind: 'Todo mês alguém precisa lembrar o cliente, mandar mensagem, enviar chave Pix, cobrar boleto atrasado' (https://www.alfadenegocios.com.br/2026/08/pix-automatico-para-pequenos-negocios.html).
first_30_days: Days 1-3: Confirm in the BCB spec which recurrence periodicities are permitted (weekly and biweekly are assumed, not yet verified) and the per-debit fee, since more frequent debits cost more per charge. Fall back to monthly with payday-aligned dates plus split mandates if not. Days 4-15: Build a thin layer over the Asaas API and a WhatsApp pre-debit rescue flow. Recruit 10 merchants from a single vertical, ideally neighborhood ISPs or courier motorbike-rental fleets, through their ERP user groups and Facebook groups. Days 16-30: Run a split test (monthly vs payday-aligned vs weekly) on new enrollments, report debit success and cancellations, and sign the first 3-5 performance-fee contracts.

title: Pre-Surveyed Superload Corridors for Data Center Freight
one_liner: A subscription library of continuously re-verified main supply routes for 100-400 ton transformer and switchgear moves, so heavy-haul carriers stop paying for a bespoke route survey on the same corridors every time.
customer: Heavy-haul carriers and project-cargo forwarders moving transformers, switchgear and generators to data centers and substations. Secondary buyers are EPC contractors, equipment OEMs and state permit offices.
problem: Every superload needs a route survey covering bridge ratings, turn radii, overhead lines, signals, rail crossings and escort rules. It costs weeks and real money, and it is repeated from scratch for the same handful of corridors from ports and rail heads to the same data-center clusters. Transformer deliveries are project cargo booked years ahead, and the domestic flatbed leg is at its tightest in years. The delay that kills schedules is rarely the bridge. It is the utility that needs six weeks and a bucket-truck crew to lift a line.
solution: Treat major corridors like military main supply routes: classify them once, then re-verify on a cycle. A survey crew captures mobile LiDAR, 360 imagery and pole-height data on a fixed corridor, then builds a route package with go/no-go strip maps and choke-point drawings. Each choke point carries the owner and the lead time to clear it (which utility, how many weeks, what it costs, which county road closures and escort rules apply). Sell annual corridor subscriptions, with an engineer-stamped per-move certification as an add-on. Recruit surveyors from retired combat engineers and route-reconnaissance veterans.
why_now: Data-center buildout is turning transformers into the pacing item. Industry reporting expects annual U.S. transformer demand to rise from roughly 1,500 units today toward 9,000 by 2030, with about 12 GW of capacity announced across roughly 140 projects for 2026 but only about 5 GW under construction. Forwarders now lock in manufacturing slots, ports and heavy-haul routes years ahead, and the trucking leg has a second lead-time problem.
revenue_model: Corridor subscription of about $15-60k a year per carrier per corridor, per-move engineer-certified route stamp of $3-10k, and data licenses to OEMs, developers and forwarders who want pre-clearance before quoting a delivery date.
non_obvious_insight: Route knowledge decays, and reuse is high. A few dozen corridors carry most loads, so a maintained library beats one-off surveys the way a pre-classified main supply route beats a fresh reconnaissance. The value is freshness (last verified date) and the choke-point ownership map, not the imagery. Carriers will trade permission to reuse survey data for a discount on their own move, which funds the first corridors.
first_30_days: Choose one corridor with a live job, such as a Gulf Coast port to a Texas data-center cluster or a feeder route into a Northern Virginia campus. Offer a friendly heavy-haul carrier a discounted survey of its actual move in exchange for the right to reuse the data. Use a rented or $30-40k rig (GNSS, laser pole, 360 camera) and 2 veterans with route-reconnaissance or heavy-haul permit experience. Package the deliverable, then sell corridor #2 to that carrier's competitors and to a transformer OEM's logistics manager.

title: Amnesty Desk: Legalizing Unpermitted Backyard Units
one_liner: Fixed-fee 'legalize your existing unit' service that is paid at closing, turning unpermitted ADUs and garage conversions into appraisable, financeable, insurable square footage.
customer: Homeowners (and heirs) with unpermitted ADUs, basement apartments or garage conversions built before the amnesty cutoff, plus listing agents who need the unit legal before it sells.
problem: Huge numbers of homes contain units built without permits. They can't be appraised as living area, financed, insured properly, or sold without discounts and buyer fear. Owners assume legalization means demolition or a full code retrofit, and city permit counters are unfamiliar with the new amnesty rules.
solution: Productized legalization. A paid feasibility scan (measured as-built drawing, life-safety checklist), then a fixed-price package covering plans, permit filing under the amnesty rules, inspection coordination and any minimal safety fixes. Offer a contingent, paid-at-escrow version for listing agents, and an appraiser-ready package that unlocks HELOCs or refinancing once legal.
why_now: California's AB 2533 took effect January 1, 2025. Cities generally must accept applications for eligible pre-2020 unpermitted ADUs and JADUs without retroactive penalties or full code upgrades, unless the unit is unsafe. Regional guidance was still being issued in March 2026. Some estimates say tens of thousands of additional units are now eligible. Local planning staff are still learning the process. More states are loosening ADU rules.
revenue_model: $1,500-2,500 feasibility and as-built fee, then an $8-15K legalization package. Alternatively a contingent fee of roughly 1% of the sale price paid at close for agent-referred listings. Referral fees from lenders and insurers once units are legal.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is city-by-city procedural knowledge, not architecture: how each of the roughly 500 California jurisdictions actually processes amnesty applications. The buyer of the outcome is often the next buyer, lender or insurer, so price and pitch it as a sale-price unlock ('an extra $80-150K of appraised value') rather than a permit fee. A database of how each city behaves is the compounding moat.
first_30_days: Pick 3 adjacent cities in one region (for example Bay Area or LA basin). Partner with a licensed architect or expediter and a measurement scanner. Build a one-page eligibility checker. Reach out to listing agents and to homeowners who have advertised unpermitted units on rental sites. Close the first 5 feasibility scans at $2,000 each and offer the first 2 legalizations at a discount for case studies.

title: Bookkeeper-Run Payee Registry Against Invoice Fraud
angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (back office x reputation network)
one_liner: Independent bookkeeping firms pool hashed vendor bank-account confirmations into a shared registry that flags fake invoices and 'new bank details' fraud at tiny businesses, then grows into a portable payment-reputation file for thin-file borrowers.
customer: Fractional bookkeeping and CFO firms serving 30-300 micro-clients ($99-500/month per firm). Later buyers are wholesalers, equipment lessors and CDFI lenders paying $3-8 per reputation pull.
problem: US payments lack payee-name verification (the UK has Confirmation of Payee; prior knowledge). AI writes flawless fake invoices and clones voices, as in Arup's roughly $25M deepfake video-call loss. Nacha's 2026 rules push originators toward risk-based fraud monitoring (prior knowledge; verify). Each bookkeeper sees only their own clients, so nobody learns from anyone else's near-miss. Separately, 22% of small firms seeking credit got nothing and solo businesses have no trade-reference file.
solution: A browser extension and API for bill-pay tools that hashes vendor name plus routing plus account and checks the registry: confirmed by N firms, flag first-time changes, and force a call-back to an independently sourced number. Confirmed payment events (on time, disputed) accrue to a per-business reputation file the owner controls and can carry between bookkeepers.
why_now: Voice cloning and AI-written invoices make payment fraud cheap. PE roll-ups of accounting firms push big players upmarket, so independent bookkeepers need shared infrastructure to compete. Bench's collapse made portability a selling point. The higher 1099 floor ($2,000 from 2026) likely means fewer W-9 and TIN collections, degrading vendor hygiene (inference).
revenue_model: $99-500/month per firm, per-pull fees from lenders and suppliers, and a revenue share back to contributing firms.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud data is a network good that big vendors cannot pool across rival software stacks, but a neutral consortium of small firms can, the way independent pharmacies and hardware stores formed co-ops. Bookkeepers already perform informal KYB on every client, so the registry monetizes knowledge they already hold.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 bookkeeping firms through a bookkeeper association or Facebook groups. Run a hashed shared registry manually (spreadsheet plus call-back desk) covering their combined 1,000+ vendors at $99/month. Record the first prevented fraud as the case study, then build the Bill.com and QuickBooks extension.

title: Human Callback Line Sold Through Credit Unions
one_liner: A staffed 'is this really my grandson?' phone line and call-screening kit for members over 70, paid for per enrolled member by community credit unions whose deposits walk out the door in voice-clone scams.
customer: Community banks and credit unions with $300M-$5B in assets and an older membership, paying about $3-6 per enrolled member per month. A secondary direct-to-family tier is $12 per month paid by adult children.
problem: Voice cloning needs only a few seconds of audio, and older adults are losing large sums to family-emergency and impersonation scams. The FBI reportedly counted about $352M in AI-linked fraud losses among people over 60 in 2025, and the FTC estimates most fraud goes unreported. Victims are shamed and rushed, and the scam's whole design is to prevent a pause. Most transfers are authorized, so banks are usually not liable, but the member's savings leave the institution and often end up in a crypto ATM.
solution: A screen-free service: one memorable number on a fridge magnet and phone sticker. Whenever anyone calls asking for money or urgency, the member hangs up and calls the line. A trained human (retired tellers, 911 dispatchers, nurses) runs a slow 5-minute out-of-band check: pre-registered family safe word, a call-back to the real relative through their stored circle, and a plain-language 'this matches a known scam script' verdict. Members with large cash withdrawals or wires get a teller prompt that says 'want to call the line first?', with the credit union's flag visible to the desk. Enrollment happens at branches and senior centers with a 20-minute family safe-word ritual.
why_now: Voice-clone scams have moved from novelty to mainstream in 2025-26. Regulators, state elder-exploitation reporting duties and the UK's mandatory reimbursement rules for authorized push-payment fraud point the direction US institutions are heading. Credit unions are competing on trust and member service against fintech, and have no good product for the fraud they cannot block.
revenue_model: B2B2C per-enrolled-member fee ($3-6 per month) with a pilot flat fee of about $2,000 per month per credit union; overage for call volume; $12 per month direct-to-family plan; optional add-on to sell to insurers of members' homes and autos.
non_obvious_insight: Against a perfect fake voice, the only durable defense is a slow, human, out-of-band ritual, and the buyer is not the senior but the institution holding the money. The scam is a deposit-flight event, and credit unions have the branch relationship, field-of-membership community ties and senior-center access to reach victims before the scammer does. Making the 'moment of doubt' land on a number people already trust is cheaper than any AI detector.
first_30_days: Pitch one sub-$1B credit union through its CEO or member-experience lead (reach them via state credit union league events and CUNA meetups). Recruit 8 retired tellers and dispatchers to staff phone shifts from home using Twilio and a shared inbox, with no engineering needed. Enroll 60 seniors from a local senior center in a 60-day pilot and log every attempted scam reported. Sell the results as a member-perk pilot at $2,000 per month.

title: Accessibility Disclosure Kit for US Independent Hotels
one_liner: A phone-based room-measurement kit that produces the accessibility details federal law requires on booking pages, before serial plaintiffs sue.
customer: US independent hotels and small groups of 30-300 rooms, franchisees, and the ADA-defence law firms who refer them.
problem: The federal hotel reservation rule (28 CFR 36.302(e)) requires booking systems to give enough detail about accessible rooms for guests to judge suitability, yet most sites just say 'ADA room'. Serial-filer suits repeat across the same properties and cost thousands each to settle. AI booking assistants also need structured answers on step-free showers and bed heights.
solution: A staff app guides a 20-minute walkthrough per room type using phone measurement and photos (door widths, turning space, shower type, bed height, grab bars). It generates compliant descriptions and a structured feed for OTAs, Google and AI assistants, then monitors listings for drift and provides a litigation-readiness pack.
why_now: Hotels are now being listed in AI assistants that demand structured attributes, and phones with depth sensing make measurement cheap. Serial-filer litigation continues, which gives the wedge and the budget.
revenue_model: USD 600-1,500 one-time per property plus USD 25-60 per month for monitoring, with rev-share to referring law firms.
non_obvious_insight: The lawsuit gets you the budget and the structured data is the moat. Detailed accessibility data is the missing input for agent booking, and accessible travel is an underserved segment.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 ADA-defence firms. Run a free scan showing what a serial filer sees on 100 hotel websites as lead-gen, and sell a USD 499 audit to 20 properties.

title: Shoot-Out Co-Own: Legal OS for Friend Homebuyers
one_liner: A co-ownership package for friend groups: a state-specific ownership agreement with a built-in Texas-shoot-out buyout, contribution-weighted equity, default rules and lender-friendly structure.
customer: Groups of 2-4 unrelated Gen Z and younger-millennial earners (friend pods, siblings, single buyers) in high-cost metros, referred by buyers' agents, mortgage brokers and credit unions.
problem: Surveys show roughly a third of Gen Z considering co-buying and about 60% of renters open to it, yet actual co-buying is rare because it is legally scary. What if someone wants out, marries, loses a job or dies? Lenders and title companies improvise, and disputes end friendships. First-time buyers now reach ownership around age 40, so the pressure to pool is real.
solution: A standardized co-ownership stack: a state-specific tenancy-in-common or LLC agreement, a scheduled shoot-out exit (one owner names a price, the others must buy or sell at it, which forces a fair price without appraisals or lawsuits), rights of first refusal, contribution-weighted equity with cure-period and dilution remedies for missed payments, and a shared sinking fund. It includes a multi-borrower mortgage broker network and a ledger that tracks each owner's cash and sweat equity. Life-event amendments handle marriage, job loss and death.
why_now: Co-buying interest is at record highs in 2026 surveys (Bank of America found about 32% of Gen Z considering it, and Rocket found about 60% of renters considering it), while median first-time buyer age hit a record near 40 in 2025. Lenders are courting co-borrowers and there is no dominant standard exit document.
revenue_model: $1,500-$3,000 per group for the legal package, $15 per month for the ledger and reminders, $1,000-$2,500 referral fees per funded loan, title and insurance affiliate fees, and a 1% fee to administer a shoot-out at exit.
non_obvious_insight: The friction is not wanting to co-buy, it is the exit. A shoot-out clause borrowed from partnership law gives every co-owner a fair way out and doubles as price discovery. Whoever owns the standard exit template becomes the SAFE-note of co-ownership.
first_30_days: Partner with five buyers' agents and two mortgage brokers in high-cost metros such as Seattle, Denver, Boston and the Bay Area. Recruit friend groups from first-time-buyer and house-hacking communities. Have a real-estate attorney draft templates for two states. Sell 10 pilot packages at $1,500, refunded if the deal does not close.

title: Ritual-Accurate Wedding Data and Audits for AI
one_liner: Commission consented, styled ceremony shoots with community elders across a dozen wedding traditions, captioned by ritual stage, and sell accuracy audits and licensed datasets to image-model builders and wedding-tech companies.
customer: Generative-image model builders, stock and creative platforms with AI-licensing programs, and wedding-tech companies building AI mood boards or visualizers. Audits are $5-15k each and dataset packs are $20-150k.
problem: Image generators still get weddings wrong outside the mainstream Western template, and research on cultural bias in image models documents mis-styled Indian weddings, misidentified Korean attire and mislocalized Nigerian scenes. Web-scraped labels are worse, since 'Indian wedding' collapses Sikh, Tamil, Gujarati and Bengali ceremonies. Couples now bring AI 'inspiration' images to photographers, and wedding-tech startups embarrass themselves with visualizers that get rituals wrong in the multi-day, high-budget segments they most want. The scarce resource isn't wedding pictures, it's correctly labeled, ritual-stage-accurate images with clean releases.
solution: Rite Right runs one- and two-day ritual shoots with paid models, real officiants and community elders as advisors (no unconsented guests, so licensing is clean), photographed by working wedding pros in documentary style. Each image gets structured metadata: tradition, region, ritual stage, garment and object names, and a community-authored accuracy checklist, with model and property releases and C2PA provenance. Product one is the audit, a 'Wedding Ritual Accuracy Benchmark' (about 50 prompts per tradition) scored by elders on public and private models. Product two is licensed packs. Photographers and advisors share in license revenue.
why_now: AI-training licensing has become a real market, since Adobe and Shutterstock run contributor payout programs for training use and Getty has an OpenAI deal. Lawsuits are pushing labs toward clean, consented data, and cultural-bias evaluation of image models is an active research area. AI wedding visualizers are proliferating, and their cultural errors are viral, embarrassing and commercially costly. Audits are cheap, fast and require no dataset, so they provide first revenue while the data business builds.
revenue_model: Accuracy audits at $5-15k each (repeat quarterly as models update), dataset licensing at $20-150k per tradition pack, and rev-share to photographers and advisors. Later: a 'ritual accuracy' API for wedding-tech products.
non_obvious_insight: The photographer who has shot 40 Sikh weddings can tell in three seconds whether a laavan sequence is wrong, and that knowledge is oral, undocumented and invisible to crowd-worker labeling. What data buyers lack is not volume but the moment-by-moment ritual sequence, and only people who stand in the room at these events can supply it credibly.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 community advisors across 3 traditions from your own network. Run one styled one-day shoot on a $4-6k budget and build a 300-image sample pack with structured captions. Build a 50-prompt accuracy benchmark, score the major public image models, and publish the results as a short report to generate inbound. Email trust and safety, data and product leads at mid-size model builders and wedding-tech companies with the report and a free 10-image sample, aiming for two paid pilot audits by day 90.

title: Callback Verification Network for Invoice-Paying Agents
angle: Pairing 1: AI agents & agent economy x Finance
one_liner: A consortium ledger of verified vendor bank details plus automated out-of-band callbacks that gives accounts-payable agents a signed safe-to-pay attestation before they send money to changed payment instructions.
customer: Bookkeeping and AP-outsourcing firms (each managing 100-300 SMB clients) and AP-automation vendors first, then mid-market controllers ($50M-$1B revenue).
problem: Business email compromise costs roughly $2.8B a year in reported US losses. Humans used to catch odd bank-detail changes by accident, but an AP agent that reads emails and PDFs will follow an instruction injected into an invoice at machine speed (prompt injection maps to 6 of 10 OWASP agentic risks). The US has no Confirmation of Payee, unlike the UK (since 2020) and the EU (Verification of Payee mandated from October 2025).
solution: An API the AP agent calls whenever bank details are new or changed. We match against a shared ledger of callback-verified details contributed by all customers, run TIN and account-ownership checks, and if still unverified place an outbound voice-agent call to the number on file from the last verified contract or W-9, never the number on the invoice. We return a signed attestation that the payment policy requires, and anything unattested routes to a human. An optional guarantee covers attested payments.
why_now: Agentic AP is shipping in 2026, Nacha's 2026 fraud-monitoring rule phases push originators to prove controls, Google's threat group documents autonomous multi-agent credential harvesting in under 6 hours, and voice agents make a verification callback cost cents instead of a clerk's ten minutes.
revenue_model: $3-8 per new-or-changed-details verification, $0.15-0.40 per payment monitored, and a guarantee premium (about 1-3 bps of attested payment value) once loss data exists.
non_obvious_insight: Agents remove the accidental friction that used to stop fraud, so the defense that works is a channel the attacker and any injected prompt cannot touch. A shared ledger strengthens with every adopter, which builds Confirmation of Payee bottom-up in a country whose banks will not build it.
first_30_days: Sign 10 bookkeeping firms that together manage 1,000+ SMB vendors. Run callbacks semi-manually with a voice agent and humans on escalation, and sell a verified-vendor book at $99 per month per client. Wire a webhook into one AP tool (Bill.com or Ramp style) so the attestation gates payment approval.

title: Renewal-Match Agent for Concession-Market Renters
one_liner: An agent that tracks true net-effective rents nearby, negotiates a renewal match with the landlord's leasing bot, and moves you if they refuse, paid only on savings.
customer: Renters in concession-heavy markets (Austin, Atlanta, Dallas, Phoenix, Florida) on 12-month leases, with destination landlords paying locator fees on moves.
problem: New tenants get free months while renewing tenants often receive above-market quotes, a loyalty tax. Concessions hit 15.8% of stabilized units (Austin 37%), and renters cannot see net-effective rent or spare the time to shop.
solution: With permission, the agent monitors net-effective prices in comparable buildings via listings and leasing-agent chats. About 100 days before renewal it sends a 'match or we move' letter with evidence and negotiates with the landlord's AI. If declined, it books tours, handles the move and collects the locator fee from the new building.
why_now: Operators now deploy AI leasing agents that can answer instantly, and agent protocols (like MCP-style interfaces) are appearing in property platforms. At 34 days to lease, landlords want to avoid turnover.
revenue_model: 25% of first-year renewal savings, locator commission from destination landlords on moves (often 50-100% of a month's rent in Texas and Georgia), and a premium lease-vault tier.
non_obvious_insight: Rental pricing has the same new-customer-discount, loyal-customer-premium structure that made insurers and telcos vulnerable to automated switching. When both sides run machines, the price reflects true clearing rather than inertia.
first_30_days: Run a manual concierge for 50 Austin renters recruited from local subreddits and apartment groups, taking 25% of savings. Log every quote and outcome and publish an 'Austin loyalty tax index' to attract more.

title: DKIM for Bank Accounts: Signed Payee Records
one_liner: A free, domain-verified payment record that suppliers publish, plus an AP plug-in that blocks any bank-detail change the supplier's own domain has not signed.
customer: Bookkeeping and accounting firms, and AP teams at 20-500 person companies on QuickBooks, Xero, Bill.com or NetSuite. Suppliers publish for free.
problem: BEC cost $3.05B in 2025, about 3.4x the $893M IC3 tags as AI-related, yet the money and attention go to deepfake detection. Bank-detail change requests still arrive by email or phone and get 'verified' by calling a number supplied in the same message. Small firms have no fraud team, and 3 seconds of audio now clones the voice they trust.
solution: A supplier proves domain control (DNS TXT plus a signed JSON file: legal name, hashed account and routing numbers, valid-from and valid-to dates, rotation contacts). A browser extension and accounting-app add-on compares any vendor bank details at bill entry and payment approval against that record. It hard-warns on mismatch and routes changes through a supplier-initiated, delayed, out-of-band confirmation flow. Every check is logged as evidence for the firm's crime-insurance social-engineering endorsement.
why_now: Cloned voices and AI-written invoices have broken the callback-and-voice-check control. IC3's 2025 numbers show BEC is still the largest business loss pool. Instant rails like FedNow and RTP make wrong payments irrevocable. Accounting platforms now have open app stores that allow a third-party control at the moment of payment.
revenue_model: $5-9 per client company per month for accounting firms, or $19-29 per AP seat for in-house teams. Suppliers are free. Later, per-check API fees from payment platforms and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: BEC is a provenance problem for one string of digits, not a media-authenticity problem. Email fraud fell when SPF/DKIM anchored trust in domain ownership, and the same move works for payee data. Selling through accountants avoids the two-sided cold start: each supplier who publishes instantly protects every customer of theirs that uses a participating firm.
first_30_days: Publish an open spec, a Chrome extension and a read-only Xero/QuickBooks add-on. Recruit 10-15 bookkeeping firms (30-100 clients each) through ProAdvisor and bookkeeper communities. For each firm, send its 20 largest vendors a five-minute publish flow. Convert 10 firms to $99/month plans.

title: Copyright-Registration Autopilot for AI Settlements
one_liner: Monthly bulk US copyright registration and an evidence vault for creators, so they are eligible when AI settlements and claims open.
customer: Newsletter writers, podcasters, photographers, illustrators and indie musicians, plus small publishers and labels, most of whom have never registered a work.
problem: In the Anthropic authors settlement (Sep 2025), only works with timely US registrations qualified, and new music and news suits (for example UMG and Sony against Suno, per the brief) follow the same logic. Registration also gates suing at all and statutory damages. Most independent creators skip it because of fees and friction, which puts them at the back of every claims line.
solution: OAuth into Substack, Beehiiv, Ghost, Bandcamp and portfolio storage. The service assembles the right group registrations (short online literary works, photographs, unpublished works, albums), files them with the Copyright Office, tracks registration numbers and deposit copies, and keeps a tamper-evident vault of first-publication evidence. A claims desk alerts users when a settlement or class definition matches their registered works. Has an attorney review the workflow.
why_now: The 2025-2026 AI settlements and suits made registration status the gating asset. Creator demand for anything that pays them from AI is high, and the Suno-Warner settlement shows deals are landing.
revenue_model: $19-39/month plus pass-through Copyright Office fees, a $99 first-year catch-up batch, and an optional 10% of recovered settlement payouts through the claims desk.
non_obvious_insight: Class-action money goes to the paperwork-ready. For an AI-era creator, registration status may be the most valuable and most neglected asset, and the boring gate is where a subscription business sits.
first_30_days: Partner with a copyright attorney to design the workflow. Pilot with 50 newsletter writers and 20 illustrators from creator communities, using a free 'AI-claims readiness audit' as the lead magnet.

title: Turn Gray-Market Retatrutide Demand Into Trial Enrollment
one_liner: Intercept people searching to buy unapproved obesity drugs and route them, screened, to active trials that pay by the qualified referral.
customer: CROs, sponsors and trial sites running obesity and metabolic trials (paying per qualified lead or randomized patient), with the consumer as the traffic source.
problem: Sponsors struggle to recruit GLP-1-naive participants because prior GLP-1 use is an exclusion criterion and 22% of households already have a user. Meanwhile, non-trial retatrutide use grew ~1.8x per quarter, 71% of traced users bought outside trials, and Australia issued a liver and kidney injury alert in Jun 2026.
solution: A compliance-reviewed 'legitimate access' site and search and social funnel that meets intent ('retatrutide', 'triple agonist'), explains the risks, pre-screens (BMI, comorbidities, naive or washout status, geography) and refers to nearby enrolling Phase 2/3 sites. It screens out people who already took unapproved product where the protocol excludes them, and sponsors pay on qualified referral or randomization.
why_now: Retatrutide's Phase 3 program and Lilly's planned Q1 2027 filing are peak-hype. FDA and Lilly takedowns (>14,000 listings) push searchers toward risk. Pills at $149 are draining the classic trial pool, so recruitment cost per patient is rising.
revenue_model: Est. $150-500 per qualified referral and $2-6k per randomized patient, paid by CROs and sites, with performance tiers.
non_obvious_insight: Enforcement cannot remove demand. The highest-intent audience in obesity pharmacology is currently monetized by gray-market vendors, while trial sponsors pay per head for exactly the same people.
first_30_days: Build three landing pages and a screener reviewed by a regulatory consultant. Register with 3-5 enrolling sites and one CRO recruiter. Spend ~$3k on search and social ads for 'retatrutide clinical trial' style queries (check ad-policy limits) and deliver the first 50 pre-screened leads on a pay-per-qualified-referral contract.

title: Blank-First Microplastics: Clean Kits and Data Forensics
one_liner: Sell certified low-shed sampling kits, blank/spike proficiency samples, and legacy-data re-analysis to microplastics labs whose glove-contaminated numbers are now in doubt.
customer: Environmental testing labs pursuing state microplastics accreditation, public water utilities that must test and report, university microplastics groups, and beverage/bottled-water QA labs. Litigation and NGO teams that need defensible numbers are a secondary buyer.
problem: Routine nitrile and latex gloves shed stearate particles that read as microplastics, adding about 2,000 false-positive signals per mm² in University of Michigan tests. Labs are 'searching for the needle in the haystack' and are unsure how much of their existing data is contaminated. Labs cannot reliably tell real microplastics from consumable-derived artifacts.
solution: 1) 'Blank-first' kits with characterized cleanroom gloves, pre-cleaned filters, slides and foil, plus lot-level FTIR/Raman shed certificates. 2) Blind spiked reference samples for inter-lab proficiency checks. 3) A data-forensics service that re-screens a lab's archived spectra and micrographs for stearate signatures, using the published discrimination approach. 4) A public 'shed scoreboard' of glove and consumable brands to build trust and inbound leads.
why_now: The Michigan glove-artifact paper appeared in RSC Analytical Methods in 2026, and it says affected datasets can potentially be recovered. California's drinking-water microplastics program (SB 1422) has adopted IR and Raman methods and plans four years of testing and reporting. Its 22-lab intercomparison flagged accuracy and precision as needing improvement, so lab demand for defensible negatives is rising just as the artifact becomes public.
revenue_model: Consumable kits at roughly $300-1,000 per kit with recurring lot replenishment. Proficiency-sample subscriptions at roughly $2-5k per lab per year. Fixed-price legacy-data re-analysis packages at roughly $5-25k, and certification-lot fees.
non_obvious_insight: In a measurement crisis the money is in negative controls, not in a better detector. The demand evidence is the University of Michigan finding of ~2,000 false positives/mm² from ordinary gloves and 'thousands of times higher than expected' counts (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/03/260329222938.htm). California's inter-laboratory study also says methods need better accuracy and precision through training and refinement (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/microplastics.html). Every lab that ever wore nitrile gloves has a reason to buy reassurance, and the researchers themselves say old datasets can be salvaged, which creates a service market.
first_30_days: Buy about 10 glove brands, filters and slides, and run shed tests through a university core-facility FTIR or Raman instrument to produce a public shed scoreboard. Write to the paper's authors and about 30 accredited environmental labs and utility QA managers. Sell the first 10 pilot kits at cost-plus and offer 2-3 discounted forensic re-analyses in exchange for case studies.
